title: Chapter XXIV
chineseTitle: 第 24 章：沙漠中的水井

paragraphs.en: Eight days after my accident in the desert, I finished listening to the merchant's story as I drank the last of my water.
paragraphs.zh: 八天后，在沙漠中的那次事故之后，我喝干了最后一口水，听完那个商人的故事。

paragraphs.en: "Ah," said the little prince, "your memories are delightful, but I still need to fix my plane and find water. If only I could walk freely toward a spring!"
paragraphs.zh: “啊，”小王子说道，“你的回忆很美好，但我还是需要修理我的飞机并找些水。要是我能自由地走向泉眼该多好！”

paragraphs.en: "My dear friend, this fox is no longer important!" I replied.
paragraphs.zh: 我亲爱的朋友，这只狐狸已经不重要了！

paragraphs.en: "Why not?" he asked.
paragraphs.zh: “为什么不呢？”他脱口问道。

paragraphs.en: "I am about to die of thirst..."
paragraphs.zh: “我快要渴死了……”

paragraphs.en: He continued, "It's good to have had a friend even if you're dying."
paragraphs.zh: 他继续说道：“即使是在生命最后一刻，能有一个朋友相伴也是好的。”

paragraphs.en: I thought, "He doesn't understand. He has never been hungry or thirsty; all he needs is a little sunshine."
paragraphs.zh: 我想：“他不懂的。他从未经历过饥饿或口渴，对他来说，只需要一点阳光。”

paragraphs.en: But he looked at me steadily and said, "I'm thirsty too. Let's find a well."
paragraphs.zh: 但他直视着我说：“我也渴。咱们找口水井吧。”

paragraphs.en: My efforts seemed futile, but we began walking.
paragraphs.zh: 我的努力似乎徒劳无功，但我们还是开始走了。

paragraphs.en: Hours passed in silence until darkness fell and stars appeared. My thirst made me feverish, and I stared at the stars as if in a dream. The little prince's words echoed: "You are also thirsty?"
paragraphs.zh: 几个小时过去，天色渐暗，星辰渐渐显现。我的口渴让我变得焦躁不安，我仿佛在梦中一般盯着那些星星。小王子的话回响在我的耳边：“你也感到口渴吗？”

paragraphs.en: He did not answer directly. Instead, he said, "Water is good for the heart."
paragraphs.zh: 他没有直接作答，而是说：“水对心脏有益。”

paragraphs.en: I didn't understand but remained silent.
paragraphs.zh: 我不明白，但选择了沉默。

paragraphs.en: Tired, he sat down, and I joined him. After a moment, he spoke again: "The stars are beautiful because of an unseen flower."
paragraphs.zh: 他疲惫地坐了下来，我也跟着坐下。过了一会儿，他开口说道：“因为那看不见的花朵，星星才如此美丽。”

paragraphs.en: I agreed, "Yes, that's true." We sat in silence, looking at the moonlit sand dunes.
paragraphs.zh: 我应声说道：“是的，确实如此。”我们默默坐着，望着月光下的沙丘。

paragraphs.en: "The desert is beautiful," he added.
paragraphs.zh: “沙漠很美，”他补充道。

paragraphs.en: Indeed, I have always loved the desert. Sitting on its sands, seeing and hearing nothing, something throbs and gleams through the silence.
paragraphs.zh: 事实上，我始终热爱沙漠。坐在沙地上，四周一片寂静，只有某种声音在沉默中跳动和闪烁。

paragraphs.en: The little prince said, "What makes the desert beautiful is that somewhere it hides a well."
paragraphs.zh: 小王子说：“使沙漠变得美丽的是，在某个地方藏着一口井。”

paragraphs.en: I was struck by his words. As a child, my old house had been rumored to hold buried treasure, though no one knew how to find it. The mystery cast an enchantment over our home.
paragraphs.zh: 我被他的话触动了。小时候，我家老宅曾被人传言藏有宝藏，但没人知道如何找到它。这种神秘感给我们的家蒙上了一层魔幻的色彩。

paragraphs.en: "Yes," I replied, "beauty lies in what is invisible—like the house, stars, and desert."
paragraphs.zh: “确实如此，”我说，“美在于看不见的东西——就像那座房子、星星和沙漠。”

paragraphs.en: The little prince smiled, pleased with my agreement. As he drifted off to sleep, I held him close and began walking again under the moonlight. His pale forehead, closed eyes, and hair swaying gently in the breeze reminded me of his fragility.
paragraphs.zh: 小王子微笑着，对我赞同表示满意。他渐渐进入了梦乡，我紧紧抱着他，在月光下继续前行。他的苍白额头、紧闭的眼睑以及在晚风中轻轻摇曳的头发，让我想起了他的脆弱。

paragraphs.en: His half-smile suggested a secret loyalty, perhaps to a flower—a rose that shone through his being like a lamp. This thought made him seem even more delicate, and I felt an urge to protect him as if he were a flame vulnerable to the slightest wind.
paragraphs.zh: 他的半笑中透露出一种隐秘的忠诚，或许是对一朵花——一束玫瑰——的忠诚。这种想法让他显得更加脆弱，我心中涌起一股保护他的冲动，仿佛他是一朵火焰，极易被微风扑灭。

paragraphs.en: At dawn, we found the well.
paragraphs.zh: 黎明时分，我们发现了那口井。
